findings.title: `include_website_name` is dead code, so `website_name` leaks the website of restricted TL0 users
findings.description:
The guard is defined as `include_website_name` without the trailing `?`. `active_model_serializers` 0.8.3 only consults `include_<attr>?`, and every other guard in this file uses that form (e.g. `include_email?` at line 117). The method is never called and `website_name` is always serialized.

- **Bypass:** `website` is in `untrusted_attributes` (line 109), which hides it when `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)` is true (TL0 user seen by anonymous, `lib/guardian/user_guardian.rb:58`). `website_name` is not in that list and reads `object.user_profile.website` directly.
- **Effect:** anonymous visitors and crawlers still receive the host (plus path on same-domain matches) for TL0 users. `user.hbs:66-72` then renders the globe icon and the name, which is the spam exposure the restriction exists to prevent.
- **Renaming alone is not enough:** the body `website.present?` does not check `restrict_user_fields?` either.
- **Fix:** add `:website_name` to `untrusted_attributes` and delete the hand-written guard.

findings.title: `website_name` goes stale on the client after a preferences save
Blanket `rescue nil` and repeated URI parsing in `website_name`
findings.description:
`URI(website.to_s).host rescue nil` swallows every `StandardError`, not just `URI::InvalidURIError`.

- **Regression:** a website that Ruby's `URI` rejects (non-ASCII host or path, embedded spaces) now yields `nil`, so the template hides the website block entirely. The old `website.split("/")[2]` still showed the host. `UserUpdater#format_url` only prepends `http://`, so such values can be stored.
- **Repeated work:** the URI is re-parsed up to three more times (lines 143, 146, 149). Parse once into a local with an explicit `rescue URI::InvalidURIError` and reuse `uri.host` / `uri.path`.

findings.title: Domain comparison is hard to follow and wrong for several host shapes
findings.description:
The three-branch comparison repeats `split('.')` five times and gives inconsistent answers:

- **Multi-label public suffixes:** forum `forum.co.uk` and website `other.co.uk` (or two unrelated `*.github.io` / `*.herokuapp.com` hosts) both have three labels and share the tail, so line 146 treats them as the same site and appends the path.
- **Asymmetric subdomains:** forum `forum.example.com` with website `example.com` shows the path, but forum `example.com` with website `blog.example.com` shows the host only. So does `forum.example.com` with `a.b.example.com`.
- **Case:** `URI#host` is not downcased, so `http://Example.com/user` on `example.com` falls through to host only.

Line 149 also uses `"." << website_host`, which mutates a string literal and would raise under `# frozen_string_literal: true`; use `".#{website_host}"`. Extracting the comparison into a small named helper would make the intent testable.
